'''Kenrich Lo Williams''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|k|ɛ|n|r|ɪ|tʃ}} {{respell|KEN|ritch}};<ref>{{cite press release |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide
 |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=October 24, 2023 |access-date=May 18, 2024}}</ref> born December 2, 1994), nicknamed "'''Kenny Hustle'''",<ref>{{cite news|last=Mendez|first=Carlos|title=Who is Kenny Hustle? TCU's, and the Big 12's, leading rebounder|url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/texas-christian-university/article126262339.html|access-date=January 25, 2019|work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]|date=January 12, 2017}}</ref> is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU Horned Frogs]] of the [[Big 12 Conference]]. After going undrafted, Williams signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in 2018, spending two seasons with the team before being traded to the Thunder in 2020, later winning an NBA championship in [[2025 NBA Finals|2025]].

==High school career==
Williams attended [[University High School (Waco, Texas)|University High School]] in [[Waco, Texas]] and joined the varsity team as a junior under coach Rodney Smith. As a senior, Williams averaged 14.6 points, 9.9 rebounds and 2.1 steals per game. He earned District 8-4A defensive player of the year honors and led the squad to a 28–5 record. Coming out of high school, Williams did not receive a single Division I offer. He attributes this to playing only one season of [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] ball.<ref name="wacotrib">{{cite news|last=Werner|first=John|title=University's Kenrich Williams turning heads at TCU|url=http://www.wacotrib.com/sports/high_schools/central_texas_boys_basketball/university-s-kenrich-williams-turning-heads-at-tcu/article_dee3567f-96bf-5448-8894-d89dc26ffe1e.html|access-date=May 19, 2018|work=[[Waco Tribune]]|date=April 6, 2017}}</ref>

==College career==
Williams attended [[New Mexico Junior College]] and averaged 10.1 points and 6.9 rebounds per game in his freshman season. He was recruited to [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]], which went winless in conference games in the season before his arrival. Williams posted 8.6 points and 6.7 rebounds per game as a sophomore on an 18–15 team. Williams missed the entire [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16 season]] due to a knee injury which required surgery, calling it one of the toughest years of his basketball career as TCU struggled to 12 wins.<ref name="wacotrib"/>

As a fourth-year junior, Williams averaged 11.4 points and 9.7 rebounds per game while shooting 49.5 percent from the floor. He had 19 double-doubles, leading the [[Big 12]], and helped lead the team to a 24–15 season. Williams had 18 points and eight rebounds in the 85–82 upset of [[2016–17 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] in the quarterfinals of the Big 12 tournament.<ref name="wacotrib"/> In the second round of the [[2017 National Invitation Tournament|2017 NIT]], an 86–68 win over [[2016–17 Richmond Spiders men's basketball team|Richmond]], Williams recorded the first [[triple-double]] in TCU history with 11 points, 14 rebounds and 10 assists.<ref>{{cite news|title=First triple-double for TCU sinks Richmond 86-68 in NIT |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400947326|access-date=May 19, 2018|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 22, 2017}}</ref> After posting 25 points and 12 rebounds in the [[National Invitation Tournament#Men's postseason NIT champions|NIT championship game]] versus [[2016–17 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]], Williams was named NIT Most Valuable Player.<ref name="wacotrib"/>

Coming into his senior season, Williams was a Preseason Big 12 Honorable Mention.<ref>{{cite news|last=Mendez|first=Carlos|title=Guess what TCU player got snubbed on the Big 12 preseason basketball team|url=http://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/texas-christian-university/article178462826.html|access-date=May 19, 2018|work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]|date=October 12, 2017}}</ref> On December 6, 2017, Williams scored a career-high 27 points in a 94–83 win over [[2017–18 SMU Mustangs men's basketball team|SMU]].<ref>{{cite news|title=No. 20 TCU extends win streak to 13 with 94-83 win over SMU|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400987995|access-date=May 19, 2018|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 6, 2017}}</ref> He sat out a game on December 22, against [[2017–18 William & Mary Tribe men's basketball team|William & Mary]], due to a knee sprain.<ref name="straka">{{cite news|last=Straka|first=Dean|title=TCU guard Kenrich Williams sustains knee injury, absent vs. William & Mary|url=https://www.springfieldnewssun.com/sports/college/tcu-guard-kenrich-williams-sustains-knee-injury-absent-william-mary/lW0xYd3EpjbzxogQQUsHOO/|access-date=May 19, 2018|work=[[Springfield News-Sun]]|date=December 22, 2017|archive-date=May 20, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180520192610/https://www.springfieldnewssun.com/sports/college/tcu-guard-kenrich-williams-sustains-knee-injury-absent-william-mary/lW0xYd3EpjbzxogQQUsHOO/|url-status=dead}}</ref> As a senior, Williams posted 13.2 points and 9.3 rebounds per game, second in the [[Big 12 Conference]]. Williams was selected to the [[USBWA]] All-District VII and [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] All-District 8 Second Team.<ref name="wilkerson">{{cite news|last=Wilkerson|first=William|title=This TCU player has been invited to NBA Draft Combine|url=http://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/texas-christian-university/article210639544.html|access-date=May 19, 2018|work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]|date=May 7, 2018}}</ref> He was named to the Second Team All-Big 12.<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://big12sports.com/news/2018/3/4/211704001.aspx |title=Men's Basketball All-Big 12 Awards Announced |publisher=Big 12 Conference |date=March 4, 2018 |access-date=October 27, 2023}}</ref> He led TCU to a 21–12 record and #6 seed in the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. In his final game as a Horned Frog, a 57–52 upset loss to [[2017–18 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]], Williams scored 14 points.<ref>{{cite news|title=Retreivers(sic) shock top seed Virginia|url=http://tdn.com/sports/retreivers-shock-top-seed-virginia/article_740d61c3-f123-55e9-aa2a-7d5679a6f4f9.html|access-date=April 11, 2018|work=Longview Daily News|agency=Associated Press|date=March 16, 2018}}</ref>

In 2024, Williams' number 34 jersey was retired by TCU.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 10, 2024 |title=TCU to Retire Williams’ Jersey
 |url=https://gofrogs.com/news/2024/1/10/mens-basketball-tcu-to-retire-williams-jersey.aspx |access-date=February 6, 2024 |website=TCU Athletics}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===New Orleans Pelicans (2018–2020)===
After going undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]], Williams signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]] for NBA Summer League play.<ref>{{cite news |last=Werner |first=John |title=University's Williams taking free agent route to NBA |url=http://www.wacotrib.com/sports/high_schools/central_texas_boys_basketball/williams-taking-free-agent-route-to-nba/article_2d84499d-6482-5320-a9fb-7f37e98f67b5.html |access-date=June 24, 2018 |work=[[Waco Tribune-Herald]] |date=June 22, 2018}}</ref> On July 24, Williams signed a deal with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Pelicans sign Garlon Green and Kenrich Williams |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-garlon-green-and-kenrich-williams |website=NBA.com |access-date=August 4, 2018 |date=July 24, 2018}}</ref> Williams later made his professional, NBA debut on October 17, 2018, in a blowout win over the [[Houston Rockets]]. During his rookie season, he was assigned to the [[Westchester Knicks]] of the [[NBA G League]], making his G League debut on November 23.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pelicans assign Kenrich Williams to Westchester Knicks |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-assign-kenrich-williams-westchester-knicks |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 24, 2018 |date=November 22, 2018}}</ref> On January 30, 2019, Williams set a new career high in scoring with 21 points, and set personal bests in field goals (eight), three-pointers (five), assists (three) and minutes (38) in a 99–105 loss to the Denver Nuggets.<ref>{{cite news |last=Brown |first=Nathan |title=Rookie Kenrich Williams' career night not enough as Pelicans fall to the Nuggets 105-99 |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/pelicans/article_36dcce8e-6af8-5a9d-962f-ede8cc719cb6.html |access-date=December 2, 2019 |work=[[The New Orleans Advocate]] |date=January 30, 2019}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2020–present)===
On November 24, 2020, Williams was part of a four-team trade in which he was sent to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web |date=November 24, 2020 |title=Thunder Acquires George Hill, Zylan Cheatham, Josh Gray, Darius Miller, Kenrich Williams, One First and Two Second-Round Draft Picks and a Trade Exception |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/hill-cheatham-gray-miller-williams-201124 |access-date=October 27, 2023 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

On July 20, 2022, Williams re-signed with the Thunder on a four-year, $27.2 million contract extension.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 20, 2022 |title=Thunder Signs Kenrich Williams to a Multi-Year Contract Extension |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-kwilliams-220720 |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=nba.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |authorlink=Adrian Wojnarowski |date=2022-07-18 |title=Sources: Thunder extend Williams on 4-year deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34264025 |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> On March 2, 2023, the Thunder announced that he suffered a left wrist injury and would undergo surgery to address the issue, ending his 2022–23 season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 2, 2023 |title=Thunder Injury Update |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/update-230302 |access-date=March 2, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

On February 7, 2023, [[LeBron James]] broke the all-time NBA scoring record whilst being defended by Williams.

On September 18, 2024, Williams underwent an [[arthroscopy|arthroscopic]] [[debridement]] procedure on his right knee.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kenrich Williams Undergoes Right Knee Procedure, Will Be Re-Evaluated After Preseason |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/277291/Kenrich-Williams-Undergoes-Right-Knee-Procedure-Will-Be-Re-Evaluated-After-Preseason |website=basketball.realgm.com |access-date=19 September 2024 |language=en}}</ref> He made 67 appearances (seven starts) starts for Oklahoma City during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 6.3 points, 3.5 rebounds, and 1.4 assists. Williams won the [[2025 NBA Finals]] when the Thunder defeated the [[Indiana Pacers]] in seven games.

On September 29, 2025, Williams underwent an arthroscopic procedure on his left knee.<ref>{{cite web | title=Thunder's Kenrich Williams: Undergoing knee surgery | website=CBS Sports | date=2025-09-29 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/thunders-kenrich-williams-undergoing-knee-surgery/ | access-date=2025-12-07}}</ref>

On July 2, 2026, Williams re-signed with the Thunder on a one-year, $5 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adams |first=Luke |date=July 2, 2026 |title=Thunder To Re-Sign Kenrich Williams |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2026/07/thunder-to-re-sign-kenrich-williams.html |access-date=July 5, 2026 |website=HoopsRumors.com}}</ref>
